g1.note: Confirmed after reading: claude-code#97272 (2026-09-25) says the auto mode classifier judges only command text, so `kubectl delete pod X --context lab` gets an avoidable prompt because safety depends on which cluster and namespace. autopilot#1125 (2026-11-03): permission rules 'only see command text', so with auto-approve or a broad allow rule nothing stops terraform destroy. soleur#9776 (2026-10-08): autonomous mode auto-approves any Bash not on a blocklist, and terraform/tofu destroy and apply -destroy pass. cognito-user-pool#443 (2026-08-10): the allowlist had to be widened to Bash(terraform:*). claude-code#103895 (2026-10-21): a user-requested Terraform Cloud apply stalled under repeated classifier blocks. #94579 is related (auto mode let a destructive remote docker command through). 5+ reports from 5 repositories and authors.

g2.note: Palisade (repo created 2026-03-18, HEAD commit 2026-03-20): a Claude Code PreToolUse hook and PATH shim intercept terraform/tofu/kubectl. Its pipeline is intercept, plan (`terraform plan`; `kubectl apply --dry-run=server -o json`), analyze per resource, decide ALLOW/REVIEW/BLOCK with OPA policies, then apply with plan-hash-bound approval tokens ('what was reviewed is what gets applied'). Policies are custom Rego with config data and include limit_change_count and namespace or StatefulSet deletion approval. That is the same core mechanism as Sn: decide from the dry-run's effect and execute exactly the checked artifact. What differs: Sn adds a per-task scope manifest the human confirms at handoff (Palisade uses static or custom policies) and covers Helm and Pulumi. A second candidate, roboticforce/agent-guardrails (created 2026-03-06), could not be checked because its README fetch was blocked.

g2.note: No tool from before July 2026 was found that binds an agent session to an explicit target set across kube, cloud and Terraform, mints creds only for it, hides global configs, and resolves each CLI command's effective target to deny anything outside the binding. Nearest partials: kindctl (2026-06-10) gives each worktree its own kubeconfig, local kind clusters only, which is Se. infrabroker (2026-06-03) mints per-operation SSH certs through an MCP broker; its Kubernetes target came 2026-07-03, after the cutoff. Ephyr (2026-03-14) is a task-scoped SSH/HTTP broker with macaroons and no kube/aws/terraform CLI binding. kubeleash (2026-05-24) is a per-context policy MCP server, not session binding. agentblindfold's private per-context kubeconfig also landed after the cutoff (2026-07-04). Teleport, aws-vault and kubie supply ingredients (short-lived certs, per-shell isolation) but not this per-session binding with per-command target resolution.

g3.note: mochi-donut (created 2026-10-28, 1 star): its 'yuzu check' resolves which cluster or account a command would touch against declared environments (kube_contexts, aws_profiles, ssh_hosts), runs as a Claude Code hook, and has `whoami` showing which account will be used. This is the per-command target resolution part of Sn, without credential minting. pi-guard-kubectl-context (2026-09-16, 0 stars) blocks kubectl unless --context is in an allowlist. agentblindfold added a private short-lived kubeconfig holding only the configured context on 2026-07-04. cloak#3 (2026-09-26) explicitly asks for a per-session context override for parallel agents.

g2.note: This is a well-known practice: Heroku-style git-push deploys keep the deployed commit as the remote ref and reject any push that is not a descendant ('non-fast-forward updates were rejected'), with --force as the override. The gist above, created 2012-05-13, shows the rejection when deploying a branch. That is the same core check as Sn: refuse to deploy when the live commit is not an ancestor of what you deploy, unless overridden. Sn's new part is putting the stamp on Kubernetes, Helm and Terraform targets plus the session id. Not counted: GitHub branch-deploy outdated_mode compares against main, not against the live commit, and Atlantis locking uses a lock until merge rather than an ancestry check. This is a judgment call.

g2.note: No tool from before July 2026 was found that parses ops output schemas, replaces secret-marked values (and their raw or base64 recurrences) with stable handles, and substitutes them only inside spawned processes. Nearest partials: secrets-router (2026-03-26) returns opaque handles for secrets fetched from a password store and resolves them in browser fill, but does not touch command output. mcp-server-kubernetes MASK_SECRETS masks Kubernetes Secret values by schema, but the masked values cannot be used as handles. pi-op (2026-04-17) redacts only 1Password values it injected itself, as in Se. opencode-stranger-danger (2026-05-13) uses detector/regex redaction, as in Se. 1Password op:// references give exec-time substitution, but only for secrets you inject yourself.

g3.note: claudepass (created 2026-09-09, 2 stars): 'Agents see Handles, never Secret values'. `cpass capture <handle> -- <command>` stores a tool's stdout in the vault and prints only the handle, `cpass run` resolves handles when it spawns the command, and output is redacted to [REDACTED:<handle>]. It is close to Sn but captures whole stdout and is not schema-aware. pi-keep-secret#1 (2026-11-01) proposes and implements deterministic placeholders for credentials in tool results sent to the model, restored in tool-call arguments before execution; detection is regex plus an LLM judge, not schema. Cratis/AI#863 asks that secrets never enter transcripts.

g1.note: warp#13560 (2026-07-10): after AI quota ran out mid-turn, commands that had executed were reported as cancelled, so the agent re-ran them and duplicated real external side effects. claude-code#86001 (2026-08-12): a tool interrupted mid-execution is reported to the model as never having run. claudexor#621 (2026-11-03): stream interruptions made the orchestrator retry the attempt from scratch after the work was already written. MCP#3394 (2026-09-27): retrying a mutating tools/call after a lost response re-executes the effect. The core of P (uncertain completion after interruption, then a duplicated mutation) is confirmed in 4 repositories. None is specifically about Kubernetes or Terraform rollouts.

g2.note: Durable execution (Temporal, repo created 2019-10-16; DBOS, 2024-07-19; LangGraph durable execution) is a well-known practice with the same core: journal the intent before the side effect and the result after it, then on recovery rely on the journal rather than model memory to avoid duplicates. prashkn/agent-durable-execution-engine (created 2026-05-17) applies this to LLM agent tool calls: intent fsync'd to a WAL before the side effect, and a replay finds intents with no result. Its README lists LangGraph, OpenAI/Vercel agent SDKs, Restate, Inngest, Temporal, DBOS and Hatchet as already doing this. no-amnesia (2026-05-11) re-injects state after Claude Code compaction. Sn's new part is narrower: infra pre/post fingerprints, plus probe-based reconciliation that blocks further mutations instead of retrying with an idempotency key.
